## The question this category answers

> How do you price and settle a claim on a fact rather than on a price — and, for the 'other' members, how do you delegate capital-allocation discretion to a named human party on-chain? Both answer questions the rest of DeFi's vocabulary was not built for.

## The category residue the original lane recorded

Two structural gaps and one measurement finding. (1) There is no element for CONDITIONAL-TOKEN SPLIT/MERGE — the state-partition of collateral into complementary contingent claims — which is the defining primitive of the entire prediction-market sector. `Py` splits along time; nothing splits along state. (2) There is no element for a CENTRAL COUNTERPARTY / clearinghouse, which is what the #1 protocol by volume in this category actually is; the vocabulary contains three symbols (`Sl`, `Bs`, `Ad`) that are DeFi's reconstructions of a clearinghouse default waterfall and none for the institution they reconstruct. (3) On resolution specifically: `Oa` covers the DISPUTE WRAPPER around Polymarket's settlement but not the settlement — the rulebook (natural-language resolution criteria plus named settlement source) is the actual product, and it is invisible. For Azuro and Kalshi, `Oa` does not apply at all: one resolves by a single trusted data provider, the other by exchange rule. Two of the three prediction markets have no expressible resolution mechanism whatsoever. On the 'other' members: DefiLlama's #9 and #12 categories by TVL ($16.5B combined) are curators and allocators, and the vocabulary has zero coverage of a delegated discretionary allocation mandate — the fastest-growing organizational form in DeFi has no symbol.

### Residue, verbatim

**Azuro** (12):

- a bettor's position is a transferable NFT carrying a payout struck against the pool; no operation splits pool collateral into complementary outcome claims and none recombines them
- a single protocol-wide liquidity pool is the counterparty to every bet, writing a non-linear event-contingent payoff, so no bettor ever faces another bettor
- the price of an outcome is the normalised inverse of the pool's virtual fund for that outcome, loaded with a spread allocated inversely to the outcome's probability under a total-margin constraint, and every bet moves the virtual funds so the odds worsen against incoming flow
- the odds struck at the moment of the bet are locked for that bettor and fix the payout, while the curve continues to move for everyone after
- each liquidity deposit is a separate leaf of a segment tree over a 2K+1 array, a Condition's profit and loss is distributed across a leaf range, and the updates are lazy — annotated at parent nodes and pushed down only when a provider withdraws
- a liquidity provider is locked for seven days from deposit and may withdraw at will thereafter
- one permissioned party creates and cancels events, seeds and reprices the sell-side odds, sets the reinforcement and margin, and then declares which outcome won
- a Data Provider must post collateral up to the total Reinforcement it expects to use across all its active markets
- the pool quotes a price to buy back an open bet before the event concludes, extinguishing a live contingent claim early
- a combination bet multiplies the odds of several legs into one payout while the pool's exposure to the combination is not the product of its exposures to the legs
- an app's share is the LESSER of 70% of the revenue it generated and a monthly cap of 50% of the spread times the bet size summed over its bets
- when the pool loses, the liquidity providers', Data Provider's and DAO's rewards go negative, while an app's share can only ever be positive or zero

**Grove Finance (Onchain Capital Allocator)** (12):

- a strategy may be funded only after Sky governance approves it through the Atlas Edit weekly cycle following a public forum round in which Grove answers voter questions; only approved strategies move to on-chain deployment
- the capital enters by minting USDS against a Sky allocation vault rather than by any user transferring assets in — the deposit is a governance-authorised credit line
- every asset the allocator controls sits in one minimal stateless proxy that holds no logic, and every movement of those assets is a call the proxy makes on a controller's instruction; funds never leave it
- only holders of a relayer role may invoke a fund-moving function, and the role is exercised by an off-chain planner that submits the transactions
- every controller operation is bounded by a rate limit that refills linearly at a configured slope up to a maximum, keyed per asset, per destination or per domain
- positions are taken in vaults whose deposits and redemptions do not settle synchronously: a request is made on-chain now and the claim is fulfilled later out of an off-chain process
- the economically decisive transfer is not between chains but from a chain into a fund administrator's register of record, where the subscription becomes an entry in a Cayman or Luxembourg vehicle's books
- the credit the capital ultimately buys is a tranche of a collateralised loan obligation, which from the allocator's position is a single opaque net asset value with no visible waterfall
- users also accrue Grove Points in proportion to their activity, which are non-transferable, have no monetary value and confer no claim or entitlement
- GROVE holders stake into stGROVE and vote directly or by delegate, but the token contract's only authorised admin is Sky's pause proxy, so administrative authority over the governance token belongs to another protocol's governance
- the Basin facility commits up to $1 billion a day of immediate stablecoin liquidity to eligible holders of tokenised funds, without purchasing or taking ownership of the underlying assets and without changing the fund's own redemption procedures, settlement cycles or transfer restrictions
- in that timelock the external issuer holds the proposal right, Grove governance executes after the delay, and a security multisig may cancel

**Kalshi** (13):

- orders rest in a continuous two-sided limit order book operated by the exchange, quoted in sub-penny dollar prices and published as bids only
- the long and short of one contract are complementary claims on one escrowed dollar, and that complementarity exists only as a price identity — a YES bid at X is a NO ask at $1.00 minus X — with no object that can be split into or merged out of the pair
- on acceptance of a matched trade the clearing house is substituted as seller to the buying participant and buyer to the selling participant, the original bilateral contract is extinguished, and the parties are released from their obligations to each other
- open margined positions are marked and settled in cash at least once each business day, with unscheduled intra-day calls available
- a scalar contract apportions the $1.00 between long and short as a function of where the Expiration Value falls, rather than paying it wholly to one side
- the operator commits two capped tranches of its own capital to the default waterfall, one ahead of the mutualised fund and one behind it, each capped at the greater of $20 million or 10% of the guaranty fund
- when the fund is exhausted the clearing house may call assessments on every surviving member, pro rata to their deposit requirement over the preceding three months, capped at 200% for one default and 550% for multiple defaults in six months, and refundable pro rata out of later recoveries
- the mutualised default fund is partitioned by Contract Segment between the fully-collateralised and margined product classes, and the collateral of non-defaulting customers in each account class may not be applied to a defaulting member's obligations
- the outcome of a contract is determined by an internal committee of the exchange with full discretion, within 24 hours, and its determination is final and not subject to review
- where the Expiration Value is indeterminable the contract may be settled at its own last traded price
- after the first day of trading the venue may designate a new Source Agency and Underlying for a listed contract and change its specifications
- a new market exists because the venue self-certified its terms with the regulator under CEA 5c(c) and the regulator did not object within the window
- customer funds are held in United States dollars only, segregated by account class under CFTC Reg. 1.20 or Part 22 with the clearing house holding a continuing first-priority security interest and UCC control over them, investable only in US Treasuries, agency securities, reverse repo on those and government money-market funds up to two-year maturity — and the clearing house retains all profit from that investment not paid to members

**Polymarket** (8):

- one unit of collateral is partitioned into one YES and one NO outcome token, and returning both recombines them into that unit, under an enforced invariant that the partition is pairwise disjoint, that no index set is empty and that none is the whole state space
- two of the three settlement modes of the matching engine are that primitive: two crossing buy orders mint a complementary pair out of collateral, and two crossing sell orders merge a pair back into collateral, with only a crossing buy against a sell settling by transfer
- the question being resolved is prose: a natural-language resolution criterion posted under the order book, against which every dispute is a dispute about text
- an admin may flag a market, which pauses it and starts a fixed one-hour safety period, after which the admin writes the payout vector directly, overriding the oracle entirely
- for a family of binary markets of which exactly one resolves true, a holder may exchange a bundle of NO positions for collateral plus the residual YES, financed before resolution out of a wrapped-collateral buffer the adapter holds itself; if the family's mutual-exclusivity constraint is violated the family cannot fully resolve and funds are frozen
- the exchange wraps that collateral a second time as PMCT through a collateral adapter with dedicated onramp and offramp contracts, so an adapter can hold liquidity outside the conditional-token accounting
- on the US venue every matched trade is novated: the clearing house is immediately substituted as seller to the purchaser and purchaser to the seller
- on the US venue a company officer runs a Contract Outcome Review Process, determines the final outcome at sole discretion, and may reverse a determined outcome in the case of obvious error, with company liability to any one participant capped at $2,500 a day, $5,000 a month and $50,000 a year

**Steakhouse Financial (Risk Curators)** (10):

- a named firm decides which markets the capital may enter, in what order they fill and drain, and rebalances at will, for a share of the interest generated
- each market carries a supply cap defaulting to zero, so no market may receive any capital until the curator explicitly caps it up, and a vault may enable at most thirty markets
- deposits fill along an ordered supply queue up to each cap and withdrawals drain along an ordered withdraw queue, so the identity of the market receiving the next dollar is a curator-set ordering
- capital not deployed into a market sits as idle supply in a market with null oracle and null collateral addresses, immediately withdrawable
- vault users become vault guardians in proportion to the size of their deposit, and may veto a critical curator action inside the timelock window
- authority is split four ways — an appointer, a strategy-setter who sets caps and fees, bounded executors who may only move funds within the strategy-setter's limits, and sentinels who may only reduce
- the fee is paid by minting new vault shares to the fee recipients, so it is borne as dilution of every other holder rather than as a transfer of assets
- the curator disclaims being a broker, intermediary, agent, custodian or advisor, disclaims any fiduciary relationship or obligation, caps total liability at $1,000, and routes disputes to Cayman arbitration with a class-action waiver
- before a market may be listed at all, at least two members of the risk team run a quality-control review across six named risk vectors, and every vault passes a due-diligence questionnaire with at least two internal and one external reviewer
- where the capital goes is a function of a published, versioned three-layer rating — an asset rating over issuer, credit and operational pillars, a platform rating, and a market rating over oracle, liquidity, price fluctuation, LLTV and credit-enhancement criteria — which is entirely off-chain

## Lane narrative

**What the section introduction should say.** The category prices and settles a claim on a *fact* rather than on a price, and it is the residual of the sampling frame — three prediction venues plus two capital-allocation businesses the lane could not file elsewhere. It has three exclusive elements, two of candidate status, and **no element present in all five members**.

**Two structural claims, both confirmed, one needing re-siting.**

- **Nothing splits collateral along a state partition.** One element splits a claim along *time*; nothing splits one along *state*. This is the defining primitive of the entire sector, and its absence takes order matching with it: two of one venue's three settlement modes *are* that split and merge, so the missing primitive removes the matching engine too.
- **There is no element for a central counterparty** — but the shape is not the one expected. That venue now runs a clearing house **with no guaranty fund at all**, so the three symbols that were said to reconstruct a default waterfall reconstruct nothing there. Two further pieces, operator first-loss tranches and callable assessments, have no symbol either.

**A refutation to carry.** One allocator has a depositor-weighted veto, which refutes "no on-chain recourse". The real distinction is **preventive versus compensatory** recourse — the depositor can stop a change but cannot be made whole after one — and that is a sharper claim than the one it replaces.

**Also.** That venue's collateral is now a wrapped dollar that arms a peg-swap element the corpus record does not carry, and one allocator's product post-dates the corpus entirely.
